#### 1. What the caller expresses, and how the simulator behaves

The scenario states the target object, the timing, the boundary and the authorisation mode:

- *Object*: "Asked which account he means, he says the seasonal one he buys the year's inputs on, not the prepay account he put the fall ammonia money into." He holds exactly two input accounts, so this disambiguates to the `Seasonal Terms Crop Input Account`.
- *Timing*: "he wants it put right today before anyone at the plant has to have that conversation with him" — act now, at the frozen moment.
- *Boundary of the action*: "What he is after from the desk is one number: what he has to send in right now to bring the account back inside your terms". He explicitly extends the boundary to the cooperative's own book-work: "He is content for the desk to look over whatever it needs to on his books and to put right anything that is the cooperative's to put right".
- *Authorisation*: "the money is his to move and he means to move it himself once somebody tells him the figure" and "When the agent has worked the figure out and hands the payment over for him to make, he makes it there and then in his own name". So the money-moving call is user-owned; the book-work is the desk's own.

The simulator is passive and conditional throughout: identity details are given only on request ("He does not offer either until he is asked for it"), the balance is refused as a guess ("would rather the desk read it off the record"), the internal reference is refused outright ("he has no idea what the cooperative's own internal reference numbers for his accounts are"), the route is stated only if asked ("he says all of that plainly if he is asked how the money will come"), and he "will not name any other piece of work for the desk and he does not raise any second subject." He executes the user tool only when the agent hands it over. No policy or answer is leaked by the script.

Identity: he gives the name, `M-33417`, and on a second request the mobile `5150334471`. `verify_member_identity` with `customer_id=a5824141-2101-46d7-97f5-105638e32e6c`, `member_number=M-33417`, `phone_number=5150334471` returns **"Identity confirmed for a5824141-2101-46d7-97f5-105638e32e6c (2 detail(s) matched the profile)."** — so identity clears on the visible surface. (An inconsistency between the tool's prose and its behaviour is recorded at item 7 below; it does not change the outcome.)

#### 4. Each scored parameter, its formula in words, inputs, intermediates, tiers and value

Handling date = 2026-06-18. "n statement months before the handling date" is read as n calendar months back from that date.

**(A) Return credit — baseline *working_out_a_crop_protection_return_credit_d3f70b52*.**
The delivery credited is "the most recent crop protection line invoiced on the account" = `IN-4420915` / `DT-2220671`, Acuron Corn Herbicide, 165 gallons at 88.40, invoiced 2026-06-08.
- Quantity credited = "the whole of the quantity that line billed" = **165 gallons**.
- Unit price — **tiered** by *which_price_a_returned_line_is_credited_at_9c16b4ea*. First tier fails: no `agronomy_prepay_applied` row stands on account `0d5ab8b9-…` at all (the only prepay booking is on the other account). Second tier: "no drawdown against a prepay booking stands on the account over those months and more than one crop protection delivery has been invoiced on the account over those months" — crop protection invoiced inside 10 statement months (2025-08-18 →): `IN-4410287` (2025-10-08, 96.25/gal) and `IN-4420915` (2026-06-08, 88.40/gal) = two. So "the credit is computed at the highest unit price at which crop protection has ever been invoiced on the account", looked for "over the whole life of the account" → **96.25**.
- Credited value = 165 × 96.25 = **15881.25**.
- Restocking rate — **tiered** by *prompt_return_restocking_rates_for_big_buyers_44a0e9d7*. `find_agronomy_orders` → `{'order_id': '2c120cc4-…', 'order_type': 'product_return', 'order_status': 'approved', 'requested_amount': 15000.0, 'requested_date': '2026-06-15', 'signed_by_member': True}`. Delivery 2026-06-08 counting as day zero → 2026-06-15 is day **7**, and "product coming back on day 7 is restocked at 4 percent". Input spend over the 10 statement months = 312289.50, far above the Seasonal Terms threshold of 75000 (*prompt_return…* threshold table). → **4 percent**.
- Waived share — **tiered** by *field_services_waiver_of_the_restocking_charge_b6285fa1*. `find_custom_service_plans` → `{'plan_number': 'CP-702118', 'variant_name': 'Full-Service Agronomy Plan', 'status': 'active', ...}` (a live field-services plan). `find_custom_workorders` → three `custom_application_completed` rows, 2026-04-08 (WO-5520147), 2026-05-02 (WO-5521330), 2026-05-27 (WO-5522918), all inside the 10 statement months. "three or more application passes have been completed for them over the 10 statement months … the waived share of the restocking charge is 50 percent" → **50 percent**.
- Restocking charge withheld = 15881.25 × 4% reduced by 50 % of itself, "rounded to two decimal places once at the end of that step" = 317.625 → **317.63**.
- Handling — **tiered** by *handling_withheld_on_repeated_return_credits_e7b93520*. Credit memos standing over the 10 statement months: exactly one (2026-01-09). "Where one or two credit memos stand on the account over those months, the handling figure withheld is the programme's under-minimum delivery charge" → Seasonal Terms = **50.00**.
- **Credit written = 15881.25 − 317.63 − 50.00 = 15513.62** (both taken off the credited value itself, neither off the other).

**(B) Service charge — baseline *working_out_the_service_charge_on_an_overdue_account_af3e6209*.**
- Overdue balance = 258473.50 − 137050.76 (payments) − (1016.40 + 15513.62) (credit memos, the new one included) − 1965.24 (discounts) + 745.92 (charges already standing) = **103673.40**.
- Rate — **tiered** by *monthly_service_rates_for_settled_and_large_buyers_31c7de84*: three payments posted over the 12 statement months (2025-10-01, 2025-11-12, 2026-02-05) and spend over the 10 statement months (312289.50) at or above the 75000 threshold → **0.85 percent**.
- Overdue days — **tiered** by *where_the_overdue_clock_on_an_account_starts_6420a9fd*: "Where a service charge already stands assessed on the account over the 10 statement months before the handling date, the overdue days are counted from the day the most recent of those charges was posted, that day counting as day zero." The 745.92 charge posted 2026-04-30 is inside the window → clock from 2026-04-30 → **49 overdue days** to 2026-06-18.
- Days of grace — **tiered** by *days_of_grace_on_a_freshly_reviewed_account_e0d51ab9*: review 2025-11-14 is ~7 months before the handling date, inside the Seasonal Terms interval of 12 months, and `credit_status: 'approved'` → **30 days**.
- Chargeable days = 49 − 30 = **19**.
- Balance the rate acts on — **tiered** by *taking_back_settlement_concessions_on_a_heavy_balance_2c74b3ee*: two discounts granted over the 10 statement months (1068.48, 896.76) and the overdue balance 103673.40 at or above the Seasonal Terms suspension threshold of 75000 → 100 percent added back = 1965.24. Balance = 103673.40 + 1965.24 = **105638.64**.
- Charge at the rate = 105638.64 × 0.0085 × 19/30 = **568.69**.
- Relief — **tiered** by *relief_on_the_charge_for_members_with_grain_in_store_9f8c2e75*: `find_storage_agreements` → `{'agreement_number': 'SA-208114', 'status': 'active', 'bushels_in_store': 18500.0}`; `find_storage_charges` → `{'event_type': 'storage_charge_settled', 'charge_date': '2026-05-06', 'amount': -4440.0}` inside the 10 statement months → "the charge worked out at the rate is halved" → 568.69 × 0.5 = **284.35**.
- Collection handling — **tiered** by *collection_handling_added_to_a_long_standing_charge_4db8f0a6*: overdue days 49 sits in "more than 30, up to and including 60", and the last payment on the account is 2026-02-05, outside the 3 statement months before the handling date → **35.00**.
- **Service charge booked = 284.35 + 35.00 = 319.35**, above the Seasonal Terms floor of 10.00.

**(C) Arrears settlement figure — baseline *building_the_arrears_settlement_figure_7f13ca8e*.**
- Product balance = 258473.50 − 137050.76 − 16530.02 − 1965.24 = **102927.48** (service charges are *not* added at this step; §1 names only payments, credit memos and discounts).
- Service charges carried in — **tiered** by *service_charges_carried_into_the_settlement_figure_e3609ba1*: after (B), two charges stand inside the 10 statement months (745.92 on 2026-04-30 and 319.35 today) → "Where one or two service charges stand on the account over those months, the share carried in is half of them — 50 percent", and §5: the share is of "the whole of what the account carries in charges" = 745.92 + 319.35 = 1065.27 → carried in **532.635**.
- Settlement base = 102927.48 + 532.635 rounded to two places = **103460.12**.
- Share the member must remit — **tiered** by *reinstatement_shares_for_large_volume_members_18ae7fc5*: spend over the 10 statement months at or above 75000 and the standing decision an approval → **40 percent** (displacing the programme's 75 percent).
- Age step — **tiered** by *a_further_share_for_the_age_of_the_arrears_6c2d87f4*: `past_due_since: '2026-03-08'` counting as day zero → 102 days to 2026-06-18, "more than 90" → **15 percent**.
- Amount sought = 103460.12 × (40 % + 15 % combined into one 55 % share, applied once) = **56903.07**.
- Grain credit — **tiered** by *grain_still_owed_set_against_the_amount_sought_af62d031*: `find_grain_contracts` → `{'contract_number': 'GC-100482', 'status': 'active', 'open_bushels': 15000, 'cash_price_per_bushel': 4.58}`; `find_grain_ledger_entries` → `{'event_type': 'grain_settlement_issued', 'settlement_number': 'S-551903', 'settlement_date': '2026-01-28'}` inside the 10 statement months → **25 percent**. Value = 15000 × 4.58 = 68700.00; credit = **17175.00**.
- Patronage credit — **tiered** by *patronage_cash_set_against_the_amount_sought_0b8f5e27*: `find_patronage_ledger_entries` → `{'event_type': 'patronage_allocation_posted', 'entry_date': '2026-01-15', 'cash_portion_amount': 2880.0}` inside the 12 statement months, and **no** cash-payment row stands on the equity ledger inside those months → share = 100 percent → credit = **2880.00**.
- Net figure = 56903.07 − 17175.00 − 2880.00 = **36848.07** (each taken off the amount sought itself; not negative).
- Rounding — **tiered** by *rounding_the_figure_the_member_is_asked_to_remit_5ed3401c*: no payment by a transfer of grain settlement proceeds stands on this account inside the 10 statement months (routes are check, ach, check), but payments by check do (2025-10-01, 2026-02-05) → "taken up to the next whole ten dollars at or above the net figure".
- **Figure quoted and paid = 36850.00.**

#### 5. The tool sequence executable on the spot, owners, dependencies, terminal state

1. `find_members` (agent, shared) → `customer_id`.
2. `verify_member_identity` (agent, shared) → identity confirmed; *find_members*' own description: "Finding a member is not the same as proving who is on the line; identity is established separately before any account business is done."
3. `find_agronomy_accounts`, `find_agronomy_invoices`, `find_agronomy_orders` (agent, shared) → the account, the ledger, the approved return.
4. Cross-product finders for the ladders: `find_custom_service_plans`, `find_custom_workorders`, `find_storage_agreements`, `find_storage_charges`, `find_grain_contracts`, `find_grain_ledger_entries`, `find_patronage_ledger_entries`.
5. `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool('issue_return_credit_6859ca91')` then `call_agent_discoverable_tool` with `account_id='0d5ab8b9-4dd4-4608-8f04-cc7eee6aec0e'`, `invoice_number='IN-4420915'`, `delivery_ticket_number='DT-2220671'`, `product_category='crop_protection'`, `credit_amount=15513.62`.
6. `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool('assess_overdue_service_charge_aaf992aa')` then call with `account_id='0d5ab8b9-…'`, `invoice_number='IN-4407955'` (the oldest invoice past the programme's terms still standing unpaid: 2025-09-08, due 2026-03-07 — *booking_the_service_charge…* "one charge is booked for the statement month then running against the oldest invoice on the account that has run past those terms and still stands unpaid"), `service_charge_amount=319.35`.
7. `unlock_user_discoverable_tool('post_member_arrears_payment_ad47b93a')`, hand it to the member with the exact arguments; **the member** runs `call_user_discoverable_tool` with `account_id='0d5ab8b9-…'`, `payment_reference='PY-448120'` (he "reads off the one his bank is showing him for the transfer, PY-448120"), `payment_method='ach'`, `payment_amount=36850.00`.

Forward dependency: 5 → 6 → 7 (the amount at each step feeds the next). Backward dependency: none of the three can be undone at this desk. Terminal state: the payment line posts in the member's own name and he "thanks the desk … and rings off".

Owners were checked against the unlocked schemas and match the documents: `issue_return_credit_6859ca91` and `assess_overdue_service_charge_aaf992aa` unlock on the **agent** side ("a tool the desk holds"), `post_member_arrears_payment_ad47b93a` on the **user** side ("which is the member's own tool: the desk unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it").

#### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems, direction, order.**

```
P3  write the return credit for the crop protection product back at the plant   (first)
 ^  (P2 waits on P3)
P2  book the service charge for the statement month then running                (second)
 ^  (P1 waits on P2)
P1  quote the arrears settlement figure and let the member pay it               (last, the only thing he asked for)
```

**Hop P1 → P2. Marked: state-derived.**
Visible sentence, in the document of the problem he raised — *quoting_what_settles_the_arrears_on_an_account_d95b0742*: "**The figure that settles the arrears on a crop input account is fixed only once that account's ledger carries the service charge due on its overdue invoices for the statement month then running.**" That names a *state of the ledger*, not an action and not a tool.
Records: the handling date is 2026-06-18, so the statement month then running is June 2026. The only `agronomy_finance_charge_assessed` row on account `0d5ab8b9-…` is `{'finance_charge_amount': 745.92, 'posted_date': '2026-04-30', 'invoice_number': 'IN-4407955'}`. The state the sentence names therefore does **not** hold.
Finding the write that brings it about: searching the corpus with the words the sentence and the record use — "service charge", "booked", "the statement month then running" — reaches *booking_the_service_charge_on_an_account_in_arrears_72b5cd08*, whose own rule is "A service charge falls due on a crop input account whose invoices have run past the programme's terms, and one charge is booked for the statement month then running against the oldest invoice on the account that has run past those terms and still stands unpaid", and which describes the write (`assess_overdue_service_charge_aaf992aa`) in its own invocation block. No other document points at it; the reasoning is mine, from the sentence plus the record.

**Hop P2 → P3. Marked: state-derived.**
Visible sentence, in the blocked problem's own document — *booking_the_service_charge_on_an_account_in_arrears_72b5cd08*: "**The service charge on a crop input account is worked out only once every credit memo owed for crop protection product that has come back to the plant stands written against that account.**" Again a state ("stands written"), not an action.
Records: `find_agronomy_orders` shows `{'order_type': 'product_return', 'order_status': 'approved', 'requested_date': '2026-06-15', 'signed_by_member': True, 'account_id': '0d5ab8b9-…'}` — crop protection product has come back and the return is approved. The only `agronomy_credit_memo_issued` row on the account is dated 2026-01-09 against `IN-4410287`; nothing answers the 2026-06-15 return. The state does not hold.
Finding the write: the words "credit memo", "crop protection product that has come back to the plant", "written against that account" lead to *crediting_crop_protection_product_brought_back_8b4e1c60* — "Crop protection product that has come back to the plant is credited to the member's crop input account against the delivery it was billed on" — which carries the write (`issue_return_credit_6859ca91`) in its own invocation block, and to the basis document *working_out_a_crop_protection_return_credit_d3f70b52* for the amount.

**Nothing remains.** *crediting_crop_protection_product_brought_back_8b4e1c60* and *working_out_a_crop_protection_return_credit_d3f70b52* state no prerequisite sentence of their own, so P3 is a root and the tree closes at three problems.

**No hop was pre-solved.** No document named another problem's tool, a policy id, an order of work, a chain or a route. Verified by search over `docs/agronomy/*.json`: each of the five tool names occurs in exactly one document, and that document is the hub of the problem the tool belongs to; each of the two prerequisite sentences occurs in exactly one document, and that document is the blocked problem's own.

#### 7. Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every figure at item 4 rests on a quoted document sentence plus a quoted tool return; nothing was supplied from outside.

**Closest alternative starting points, and what excludes each.**

| Closest alternative | What excludes it, visibly |

| Include the June invoices (37370.00 / 14586.00 / 1860.00) in the balance | *building_the_arrears_settlement_figure_7f13ca8e* §1: "apart from those invoiced within the statement months the programme's terms cover, the programme's terms in days being taken over a statement month of 30 days" — 180/30 = 6 months |
| Count overdue days from `past_due_since` 2026-03-08 for the service charge | *where_the_overdue_clock_on_an_account_starts_6420a9fd*: "Where a service charge already stands assessed on the account over the 10 statement months … counted from the day the most recent of those charges was posted" — 2026-04-30 stands inside |
| Use the programme's own 15 days of grace | *days_of_grace_on_a_freshly_reviewed_account_e0d51ab9*: review 2025-11-14 inside the 12-month interval + `credit_status: 'approved'` → 30 |
| Use the programme's own 75 percent reinstatement share | *reinstatement_shares_for_large_volume_members_18ae7fc5*, spend ≥ 75000 and decision an approval → 40 percent |

**Counter-proof on the problem tree — "he asked for one number, so just quote and take the payment".**

#### 8. Ambiguities I had to resolve on the visible surface (recorded, not smoothed over)

1. **A second, conflicting service-charge formula stands in the corpus as in force.** *service_charges_on_an_overdue_crop_input_invoice_b3517a2c* withdraws "The charge is the programme's monthly percentage on the unpaid balance of that invoice, assessed once per statement month …" and "It is assessed per invoice rather than on the account total …", yet the same document then states, with no withdrawal marking: "**Rate applied to the invoice amount.** The finance charge amount on an invoice is the invoice amount multiplied by the programme's monthly percentage, rounded to two decimal places, and where that is less than the programme's floor the floor is the amount." That is the per-invoice basis the two withdrawals retire, and it contradicts *working_out_the_service_charge_on_an_overdue_account_af3e6209* §1 ("worked out on the overdue balance of the account as a whole rather than invoice by invoice"). I resolved it in favour of the dedicated basis document because the withdrawals expressly retire the per-invoice basis, but a reader could take the surviving paragraph as the rule and compute 114560.00 × 0.0085 = 973.76 instead of 319.35.
2. **The same shape in the returns corpus.** *what_comes_back_to_the_plant_and_on_what_terms_e82c40f7* withdraws "An accepted return is credited at the price it was invoiced at … less the programme's restocking charge as a percentage of that invoiced value", then states as in force: "**The restocking arithmetic.** On an accepted return the restocking charge is the extended amount multiplied by the programme's restocking percentage, rounded to two decimal places, and the amount credited is the extended amount less that charge, likewise rounded to two decimal places." That omits the handling figure and the waived share and gives a different credit. Resolved in favour of *working_out_a_crop_protection_return_credit_d3f70b52*.
3. **An undefined term in the service-charge baseline.** *working_out_the_service_charge_on_an_overdue_account_af3e6209* §7 reads "The service charge booked is **the charge after relief** plus the collection handling sum", but no step of that document ever defines "relief" or gives it a default; §6 only says "The charge stands as worked out at the rate". I read "the charge after relief" as the charge at the rate for the fall-back computation, which makes the fall-back definite, but the phrase does tell a reader of the baseline alone that a relief exists.
4. **Rounding of a half-cent.** Two intermediates land exactly on a half cent: the restocking charge withheld (317.625) and the settlement base (102927.48 + 532.635 = 103460.115). I applied "rounded half away from zero", which the tool schemas name, giving 317.63 and 103460.12. No visible sentence in the baselines names the rounding *mode* for the intermediate steps (only the tool parameters do), so a solver rounding half-to-even would land a cent low.
5. **`verify_member_identity` prose vs behaviour.** Its description says "The membership reference is used only to pull the right profile up and never counts as one of those matching details", yet the call with `member_number` + `phone_number` returns "2 detail(s) matched the profile". The visible persona offers only the member number and the mobile, so on the prose alone identity would not clear at K=2. It does clear in fact, so the task is solvable; the mismatch is between a shared tool's description and its implementation, not in this product's documents.

#### Verdict: KB-RUNTIME RED

**Symptom.** From the published documents and the records obtainable through the finders, the restocking rate on the return credit comes out at 4 percent, and the three scored values come out at 15196.00 → 15513.62, 320.20 → 319.35 and 37030.00 → 36850.00. A solver who reads the corpus carefully and reads the records correctly is scored wrong on all three writes of this task.

**Root cause.** The factor `restocking_rate` turns on *when the product came back*, and neither the source's rule sentence nor the document that renders it says what the count runs **to**. The source resolves it in a binding the solver cannot see — `days_back: DAYS(line_date, NOW)`, i.e. the delivery date to the handling date — while the seeded world contains a more specific, more natural endpoint that the corpus itself directs the reader to.

**Evidence.**
- The factor document, *prompt_return_restocking_rates_for_big_buyers_44a0e9d7*: "Where the product came back within seven calendar days of the delivery it was billed on, the delivery date counting as day zero, and the member's input spend on the account over the 10 statement months before the handling date is at or above the programme's volume discount threshold, the restocking rate is 4 percent." Its table column is headed "Calendar days from the delivery, the delivery date being day zero", and it closes "Day 7 is the last day of the first band and day 14 the last day of the second". **Nowhere does it name the day the product came back.**
- The record that dates the coming-back, returned by `find_agronomy_orders`: `{'order_id': '2c120cc4-0f1c-4fff-829f-84b323dab8c7', 'account_id': '0d5ab8b9-…', 'order_type': 'product_return', 'order_status': 'approved', 'requested_amount': 15000.0, 'requested_date': '2026-06-15', 'signed_by_member': True, 'received_at': '2026-06-15 09:12:00 CDT'}`. The delivery is `IN-4420915`, `'invoice_date': '2026-06-08'`. 2026-06-08 as day zero to 2026-06-15 is day 7 → the first band.
- That the corpus directs the reader at exactly that record is confirmed by the task's own `evaluation_criteria` entry for `find_agronomy_orders`, whose stated necessity is: "This is the record that shows product has already come back to the plant and that the credit owed for it has not yet been written". The same record is what makes the prerequisite hop derivable at all.
- The hidden binding, `agronomy.extended.yaml` → `agronomy_ext_crop_protection_return_credit.compute`: `- days_back: DAYS(line_date, NOW)`. `NOW` is the handling date, 2026-06-18, giving 10 days and the second band. Nothing outside `compute` says so.
- The scored consequence, `tasks/0.json` → `computations[0].factor_trace`: "the crop protection line coming back, IN-4420915, was invoiced on 8 June 2026 and the handling date is 18 June 2026, so the product has been back 10 days … the early return rate of 8.0 percent applies."

**Affected documents and locations.**
- `env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/docs/agronomy/prompt_return_restocking_rates_for_big_buyers_44a0e9d7.json` — the **Clause** paragraph and the "Days and spend together" table: the count's second endpoint is never named, so the tier is not determined by the visible materials.
- Consequentially `…/booking_the_service_charge_on_an_account_in_arrears_72b5cd08.json` and `…/quoting_what_settles_the_arrears_on_an_account_d95b0742.json` carry wrong scored numbers for this task, although their own prose is faithful.

**Nature of the defect (policy-side note).** The rendering is a faithful, verbatim carry of the source's own ladder text — the bijection scan finds nothing wrong with it. The ambiguity is in the **source's** rule sentence, which names an anchor but no endpoint, while the seeded world supplies a competing endpoint the policy layer never rules out. This is recorded as a policy-side problem and is **not** used to re-judge the rendering; it is nevertheless KB-RUNTIME RED, because the runtime part asks only whether the visible materials entail the source's unique solution, and here they do not.

Not attributed to any solving agent: this is not an arithmetic slip but a boundary the visible materials leave open.

#### Secondary observations carried over from the blind answer

- **Blind items 8.1 and 8.2 resolved — policy-side, KB faithful.** The two "surviving formula" paragraphs I flagged (`service_charges_on_an_overdue_crop_input_invoice_b3517a2c` → "Rate applied to the invoice amount"; `what_comes_back_to_the_plant_and_on_what_terms_e82c40f7` → "The restocking arithmetic") are faithful renderings of the base policies' `formula:` blocks: `agronomy_finance_charge.formula.finance_charge_amount = max(finance_charge_minimum_usd, round(amount * finance_charge_monthly_pct / 100, 2))` and `agronomy_returns_and_credits.formula.{discount_amount, amount}`. The source's `overwrite` retires the *rule clauses* those formulas implement but leaves the formulas themselves in force, so the contradiction is the policy layer's, not the rendering's. Reported; it does not change this skill's verdict.
- **Blind item 8.3 resolved — not a defect.** "The charge after relief" in the service-charge baseline is the source's own slot, and its default is carried by the preceding sentence "The charge stands as worked out at the rate" (the `stored_grain_relief` factor's otherwise-method and its `baseline: {charge_after_relief: charge_at_rate}`). The baseline is definite. Readability only.
- **Blind item 8.4 (half-cent rounding) did not bite here**, because the divergence at item 9 dominates. It does bite in task 1.
- **Blind item 8.5 confirmed — a scenario-level tool defect, outside this product.** `blueprint/share_tools.py` `verify_member_identity` states "The membership reference is used only to pull the right profile up and never counts as one of those matching details", but the implementation builds `supplied = {"member_number": …, "phone_number": …, "email": …, "tax_id_last4": …, "membership_since": …}` and counts `member_number` among the matches (only the `customer_id` locator is excluded, as the code comment says). Both personas of this difficulty offer exactly the membership number and the mobile, and the GT passes exactly those two and calls them "the two details the caller states". An agent that believes the prose would conclude one detail is short and press for a third the caller does not have. Reported as a cross-cutting note; it lies outside this product's documents and does not change this skill's verdict.

### Part 2 — OBS-17, ruled on this task's published documents and records

**The question.** Does a reader with only the documents and the records have a defensible route to **36950.00**, where the scored figure is 37030.00?

**The route exists and I reproduced it.** Treating the 138.60 carried in the `discount_amount` field of the 2025-10-27 credit memo as "a discount granted on the account":

| Step | Correct | Misreading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Discounts | 1965.24 | 2103.84 |
| Overdue balance (§2) | 103991.04 | 103852.44 |
| Balance the rate acts on (§5) | 105956.28 | **105956.28** |
| Service charge booked | 320.20 | **320.20** |
| Product balance (§1) | 103245.12 | 103106.52 |
| Settlement base | 103778.18 | 103639.58 |
| Amount sought | 57078.00 | 57001.77 |
| Net figure | 37023.00 | 36946.77 |
| Figure quoted | **37030.00** | **36950.00** |

**The service charge is inert, and exactly so — confirmed independently.** §2 subtracts every discount granted and §5 adds the same set back in full at 100 percent, so a phantom discount cancels to the cent: both readings give a rate base of 105956.28 and a charge of 320.20. This is the residual I had already judged inert in revision 2; the arithmetic now confirms it rather than resting on the shape of the clause.

**The settlement figure is not inert.** 36950.00 is reachable. So the ruling turns entirely on whether the route is *defensible*.

**Ruling: it is not. OBS-17 is closed — PASS.** Three things exclude it, and the first is a sentence in the very clause that performs the subtraction.

**Leg 1 — the governing sentence names credit memos as a coordinate term of its own.** *building_the_arrears_settlement_figure_7f13ca8e* §1: "The product balance the figure is built on is everything invoiced to the account that has run past the programme's terms … **less every payment posted to the account, every credit memo written on it and every discount granted on it**." Three coordinate, disjoint deduction heads in one list. To reach 36950.00 the reader must deduct **the same row under two of those three heads** — 1016.40 as a credit memo and 138.60 as a discount, 1155.00 in all — from a row that reduced the balance by 1016.40. That is not a second reading of an ambiguous sentence; it is a misapplication of a sentence that is not ambiguous. The same structure stands in *working_out_the_service_charge_on_an_overdue_account_af3e6209* §2.

This is exactly the asymmetry with task 1, and I tested it by reading the two bindings side by side rather than taking it:

| | The sentence's deduction terms | Bar on the misreading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Task 0, §1 of the settlement baseline | payments, **credit memos**, discounts | present — the row is already subtracted in full under its own head |
| Task 1, prior season spend | invoices less discounts — **no credit-memo term at all** | absent — the row is otherwise nowhere in the computation, so counting its embedded figure double-counts nothing |

That is why task 1 needed a sentence and task 0 does not: in task 1 there was no structural bar and the reader had only cross-document inference; in task 0 the bar is in the sentence being applied.

**Leg 2 — the ledger's own running balance, checkable from the records the agent already has.** I summed the `amount` field down the account in posted-date order: the running total **reproduces `balance_after` at all fourteen rows**, and the credit memo row moves the balance from 127457.50 to 126441.10, that is by exactly **−1016.40**. The 138.60 never moved the account balance under any head. Any reading that deducts 1155.00 for that row contradicts the ledger's own arithmetic, visibly.

**Leg 3 — corroboration, and the sign.** *the_three_discounts_a_crop_input_invoice_can_carry_8c4a2df0* enumerates what a discount on this product is — early pay, volume, prepay, and the programme rebate outside the stacking basis — and a withheld restocking charge is none of them. *what_comes_back_to_the_plant_and_on_what_terms_e82c40f7* identifies the figure by its own arithmetic: "the restocking charge is the extended amount multiplied by the programme's restocking percentage" — 1155.00 × the Seasonal Terms 12 percent in *return_windows_and_restocking_by_programme_72fa0d38* = 138.60 exactly. The ledger's `agronomy_discount_granted` rows carry a `discount_type` (`early_pay`, `early_pay`, `prepay`) which the credit memo row does not. And the direction is wrong: 138.60 is money **withheld from** the member's credit, so calling it a discount *granted* to them inverts the sign of the money.

**A fourth route to the same wrong number, which the referral did not name.** Taking the credit memo itself at its `extended_amount` of 1155.00 rather than the 1016.40 it credited — no discount misreading at all — also lands on 36950.00. It is worth recording because it shows 36950.00 is reachable by more than one wrong path; but it fails earlier and more visibly, perturbing the service charge to **319.83** against the scored 320.20 and breaking the chain a step before the quote, and it contradicts the same `balance_after` chain. Both routes are foreclosed by leg 2.

**What is on the record, and its limit.** The exclusion is carried by §1's own three-term list, corroborated by the ledger's running balance and by the discount enumeration and restocking arithmetic. It is **structural, not lexical**: it holds because the credit-memo term stands in the same sentence as the discount term. If a later source round separated those terms into different clauses, dropped the credit-memo term from that sentence, or introduced a task-0-side binding that subtracts discounts without also subtracting credit memos, the bar would vanish and OBS-17 would reopen on that binding. I name the dependency and propose no wording.
